correctness.rationale: The arbitrary-field classification reduces finite-field Type II algebras to anisotropic symmetric forms paired with alternating forms. Perfectness in characteristic two forces active dimension one; Chevalley--Warning forces active dimension at most two in odd characteristic. Binary zero-bracket forms have one similarity class, while mixed binary pairs are classified by the exact nonsquare invariant kappa=-det(omega)/det(beta). Counting the idempotent and zero-summand choices gives the stated N_q(n). Characteristic subspaces P^2 and Ann(P) force the triangular automorphism form; the active similitude groups have orders q-1, 2(q^2-1), and q^2-1, yielding the displayed automorphism orders.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The Plakosh--Pypka structural classification, contemporaneous low-dimensional Poisson normal forms, and general bilinear-form theory are prior work and explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. Targeted searches found no prior finite-field all-dimension enumeration, stable q+5 formula, mixed-class count in all dimensions, or automorphism-order table for Dedekind Poisson algebras.

value.rationale: The result turns a structural arbitrary-field classification into explicit finite-field moduli: the number of classes stabilizes at 4 in even characteristic and q+5 in odd characteristic, with complete mixed-class counts and automorphism orders for every class.
